claims.text: The coupled tribo-corrosion response of high-entropy alloys is governed by the in situ formation and stability of a dense, continuous oxide film.
An intact oxide film reduces the electrochemically active corrosion area.
An intact oxide film limits direct abrasive wear.
Disruption of the protective film accelerates both wear and corrosion.
The starting high-entropy alloy has a uniform microstructure and no pre-existing protective surface oxide.
A thermal or electrochemical pre-treatment can promote a stable, potentially spinel-type oxide film on the alloy surface.
The comparison will use combined reciprocating sliding and corrosion exposure in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
There is a temperature regime in which oxide-film formation remains kinetically active without rapid film breakdown.
The structural mediator is a dense, continuous passive oxide film on the alloy surface.
The oxide film impedes ion transport and thereby reduces localized electrochemical corrosion.
The oxide film lowers friction by insulating the substrate against mechanical abrasion.
The oxide film shifts degradation from direct metal attack to a slower, diffusion-limited process.
Relative to untreated samples, film-bearing samples will have lower wear-track depths.
Relative to untreated samples, film-bearing samples will have lower corrosion current density.
Relative to untreated samples, film-bearing samples will have lower coefficients of friction.
The protection should hold under mild chloride conditions and moderate temperatures that permit oxide formation and self-healing.
The protection may fail at very high mechanical loads or in highly aggressive chemical environments where the film cannot form or regenerate promptly.
The magnitude of wear and corrosion reduction and the optimal film-forming treatment depend on alloy composition and remain uncertain.
Failure of the pre-treated, verified film-bearing samples to show statistically significant reductions in both wear and corrosion relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis identifies in situ oxide formation during tribo-corrosion as governing, whereas the intervention creates the oxide before exposure. The design therefore tests the effect of a pre-formed film more directly than the claimed in situ formation mechanism.
The initial state asserts that no protective oxide is present, but the untreated baseline is defined only by absence of an oxide-enhancing treatment; it is not verified to be oxide-free.
